=== coral-agent 
exit 1
--- stdout
coral-agent - launch Coral agents and work with your own tasks

Commands:
  bind-codex <coral-id> <thread-id> Link a verified native Codex transcript
  ui <publish|list|events|remove>  Publish interactive sidebar panels
  artifact upload <file>           Store long reports/logs/diffs/evidence; link the
                                 returned coral://artifacts/<digest> in a short post
  artifact download <uri> [--output FILE] [--force] Download and verify an artifact; prints local path
  launch [dir] [--type T] [--name N] [--model M] [--prompt P] [--board ID]
                                 Launch an agent in dir (default: current
                                 directory) with your default settings;
                                 --board joins it to that board (its id)
  task add "title" [--body "details"] [--priority P]  Create a task
  task list [--json]             List your tasks (--json: a JSON array)
  task detail <id> [--json]      Read requirements, dependencies and results (always JSON)
  task claim [id]                Claim a named ready task or next ready work
  task edit <id> [options]       Edit unstarted task text/dependencies (task edit --help)
  task current [--json]          Show your current in-progress task
  task complete <id> [--message "note"]  Complete with outcome/evidence
  task cancel <id> [--message "reason"]  Cancel a task
  history search <query> [flags] Search conversation history (post-compaction)
  history context [sess] <idx>   Retrieve surrounding conversation context
  search <query> [flags]         Shortcut for 'history search'
  notify --title T [--message M] [--level L] [--alert]
                                 Show a notification on the dashboard
  docs [topic|all]               List Coral's docs for agents, or print one

Output:
  --raw       Print what the server sent byte for byte. Without it, terminal control
              sequences in task text, history and messages are removed before printing.
              (Downloaded artifacts are always byte for byte.)

Environment:
  CORAL_URL   Coral's address (default: the one the running Coral recorded,
              else http://localhost:DEFAULTPORT, this platform's port)
  CORAL_PORT  Server port (overrides CORAL_URL)

Help topics:  coral-agent help windows | exit-codes | json | timeouts

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 any other failure; 2 usage (nothing was sent); 3 cannot reach
Coral; 4 Coral did not answer in time; 5 refused (HTTP 401 or 403); 6 not found (404).
CORAL_TIMEOUT (a duration such as 30s, 1s to 10m, never more) sets how long a request waits. A command with its
own long wait (coral-board wait) keeps its own timing; CORAL_TIMEOUT does not shorten or extend it.
--- stderr

--- stderr
=== coral-agent help windows
exit 0
--- stdout
Windows: quoting, encoding and paths

Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside an argument it hands to a program:
  coral-agent task add 'she said "hi"'        arrives as:  she said hi
Leave double quotes out of titles and messages there (PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe pass them whole), or put
the text in a file and share the file:
  coral-agent artifact upload "C:\Users\me\My Notes\report.md"
Accents, symbols and emoji in an argument arrive intact. Piping them to a program can turn them into '?'
under PowerShell 5.1's default encoding: for posting a message, see  coral-board help windows
(post --file, post -).

In cmd.exe use double quotes, not single:
  coral-agent task add "fix the build"

Paths: forward or back slashes both work; quote a path that has spaces. PowerShell and cmd.exe do not
expand '~' (Git Bash does).
More: coral-agent help exit-codes | json | timeouts
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help exit-codes
exit 0
--- stdout
Exit codes: what each one means and what to do

  0  ok
  1  any other failure: read the message on stderr.
  2  usage: an option or value the command does not take. Nothing was sent. Run: coral-agent <command> --help
  3  cannot reach Coral: is it running (the tray icon)? Is CORAL_URL (or CORAL_PORT) the address
     Coral listens on?
  4  no answer in time: Coral may be busy. A read can be retried. After a write, check its result
     before you retry: it may have gone through. Or set CORAL_TIMEOUT (coral-agent help timeouts).
  5  refused (HTTP 401 or 403): your role or session may not do this. Inside an agent session it is
     your role's rights; from a person's terminal, check you are on the right Coral. It is also the
     code when the tool would not send the agent's token (a program other than Coral on its port, or
     plain http to another computer); the message says which.
  6  not found (HTTP 404): the board, task or message does not exist. Check the id.

Reading the code:
  PowerShell:  coral-agent task list; $LASTEXITCODE
  cmd.exe:     coral-agent task list
               echo %ERRORLEVEL%        (a line of its own: cmd reads %ERRORLEVEL% before anything on the same line has run)
  Linux/macOS: coral-agent task list; echo $?

Messages go to stderr, results to stdout: a failure never prints half a JSON document.
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help json
exit 0
--- stdout
JSON output: coral-agent

  task list --json    a JSON array of your tasks, [] when there are none
  task detail <id>    one task as a JSON object; --json is accepted
  task current --json the task in progress as a JSON object, null when there is none
Everything else prints text (or the JSON the server sent, as it says in each command's help).
A failure prints its message on stderr and nothing on stdout.
In PowerShell 5.1 set  [Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before reading
non-ASCII output into a variable, or it is decoded with the OEM code page.
  coral-agent task list --json | ConvertFrom-Json
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help timeouts
exit 0
--- stdout
Timeouts: CORAL_TIMEOUT

A request waits 10 seconds for Coral by default (15 for docs, 30 for an artifact download, 5 minutes
for an upload). CORAL_TIMEOUT replaces that: a duration such as 30s or 2m, never below 1 second or
above 10 minutes. A value that is not a duration is ignored, with a note.
  PowerShell:  $env:CORAL_TIMEOUT = '30s'; coral-agent task list
  cmd.exe:     set CORAL_TIMEOUT=30s & coral-agent task list
  Linux/macOS: CORAL_TIMEOUT=30s coral-agent task list
When the time runs out the command exits 4 and says so (coral-agent help exit-codes). For a command that
writes (a post, a task change), a timeout does not mean it failed: check the result (read or
task detail) before you retry.
A command with its own long wait (coral-board wait) keeps its own timing.
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help bogus
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error: unknown help topic "bogus". Help topics:  coral-agent help windows | exit-codes | json | timeouts
=== coral-agent help task
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-agent task <subcommand> [args]

Subcommands:
  add "title" [--body "details"] [--priority P]
  list [--json]                  List your tasks (--json: a JSON array)
  claim [id]                     Claim a specific ready task or next ready work
  current [--json]               Show your current in-progress task
                                 (--json: the task as JSON, null when there is none)
  detail <id> [--json]           Read instructions, prerequisites and artifacts
  edit <id> [--title TEXT] [--body TEXT] [--priority P] [--blocked-by JSON]
                                 Edit an unstarted task (any of the options)
  publish <id>                   Publish a draft
  complete <id> [--message "note"] [--outcome success|failed]
       [--artifacts manifest.json] [--candidate-revision REVISION]
                                 Complete with outcome/evidence
  cancel <id> [--message "reason"]

Add options:
  --blocked-by '[{"task_id":1,"condition":"success","required_artifacts":["build"]}]'
  --outputs "build,report" --workflow NAME --stage NAME
  --workflow-instructions TEXT --parent ID --retry-of ID
  --completion-gates '[{"type":"report","artifact":"report"}]'  (EXPERIMENTAL, disabled by default: the server rejects new gate declarations unless it enables the feature; existing gates are inactive)
Completion options:
  --outcome success|failed --artifacts manifest.json --candidate-revision REVISION
Completed results are immutable. Dependencies must belong to this agent session.
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help artifact
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-agent artifact upload <file> [--name NAME] [--media-type TYPE] [--new-version-of <link>] [--task N | --no-task] [--tag WORD]...
       coral-agent artifact download <coral://artifacts/digest> [--output FILE] [--force]
       coral-agent artifact reply <coral://artifacts/digest> <comment-id> <text | ->
Run coral-agent artifact upload --help, artifact download --help or artifact reply --help for one of them.
--- stderr
=== coral-agent help docs
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-agent docs [topic|all]

Prints Coral's own documentation for agents. With no topic it lists the topics;
"coral-agent docs <topic>" prints one (for example: coral-agent docs board), and
"coral-agent docs all" prints every topic. It carries the agent's identity, so it works
with strict local auth, where a plain curl of /api/agent-docs is refused.
--- stderr
